title: A finite colimit algebra has a finite image-subalgebra model
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set. Let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(D_i)_{i\in I}$ be directed systems of commutative rings, with compatible homomorphisms $S_i\to D_i$ (every transition square commutes). Suppose every $D_i$ is integral over $S_i$, meaning that each element satisfies a monic polynomial over $S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Put $S=\varinjlim_i S_i$ and $D=\varinjlim_i D_i$, with their canonical compatible $S$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Assume $S$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $D$ is finite as an $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there exist $i\in I$ and an $S_i$-subalgebra $H\subseteq D_i$, finite as an $S_i$-module, for which the canonical multiplication map
$$H\otimes_{S_i}S\longrightarrow D,\qquad h\otimes s\longmapsto \bar h s,$$
is an isomorphism of $S$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Here an $S_i$-subalgebra is a subring containing the image of $S_i$ with its induced algebra structure. No injectivity, flatness, normality or finite presentation of the transition maps, and no Noetherianity of the rings $S_i,D_i$, is assumed. The conclusion concerns one finite subalgebra $H$ of a stage, not the whole ring $D_i$.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, finite generators and relations proof, combined with Tag 00GM, lemma-characterize-integral; image-subalgebra refinement written by the agent.

proof.text: Choose finite $S$-module generators of $D$. They also generate it as an $S$-algebra, since their $S$-linear span already contains every element. Thus $D$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] and choose a presentation $D\cong S[X_1,\ldots,X_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Write $d_a$ for the image of $X_a$ in $D$. The presentation generators need not be the original module generators.

source.place: Tag 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), part (3); Tag 05N9, proof of (1), choice of finite presentation

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1) separately to the diagrams $S_i$ and $D_i$. Lift all $d_a$ and all coefficients occurring in the finite list $f_b$. Choose a common upper bound $i_0$ of these finitely many stages, transporting the lifts by the transition maps. Denote the resulting elements by $x_a\in D_{i_0}$ and the lifted polynomials by $g_b\in S_{i_0}[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$. Then $x_a$ maps to $d_a$, and coefficientwise $g_b$ maps to $f_b$. A finite set has a common upper bound by repeated directedness; for an empty set choose any stage using nonemptiness.

source.place: Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), finite generators and relations proof; image-subalgebra refinement by Q82

proof.text: For each $b$, evaluation $g_b(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ maps to $f_b(d_1,\ldots,d_n)=0$ in $D$: ring maps preserve the finite sums and products in a polynomial, and the transition squares commute. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](2), comparing this evaluation with $0\in D_{i_0}$, it vanishes at some later stage. Choose one $i\geq i_0$ where all these finitely many evaluations vanish. Transport the $x_a$ and the $g_b$ there and keep the same notation. The resulting equations $g_b(x)=0$ hold in $D_i$. If $m=0$, take $i=i_0$.

source.place: Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), finite generators and relations proof; image-subalgebra refinement by Q82

proof.text: Let $H=S_i[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subseteq D_i$, the image of polynomial evaluation over $S_i$. Every $x_a$ is integral over $S_i$ by the hypothesis on $D_i$. Hence [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring] makes $H$ a finite $S_i$-module. It contains the image of $S_i$ by construction, including when the structural map is not injective. The equations $g_b(x)=0$ also hold in $H$, since its inclusion into $D_i$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00GM (lemma-characterize-integral), finite-adjoin argument in its proof

proof.text: Put $T=H\otimes_{S_i}S$. The two compatible maps $H\to D$ and $S\to D$ define the $S$-algebra map $\phi:T\to D$, $h\otimes s\mapsto\bar h s$, by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Evaluate $S[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ in $T$ at $X_a\mapsto x_a\otimes1$. Each $f_b$ evaluates to $g_b(x)\otimes1=0$: the lifted coefficients move between tensor factors by the balancing relation. This defines an $S$-algebra map $\psi:D\to T$ using the chosen presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Explicitly, send the class of $p$ to this evaluation of $p$; if $p-p^{\prime}=\sum_b q_b f_b$, their evaluations differ by $\sum_b q_b(x\otimes1)\,0=0$, so the map is well defined.

source.place: Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), finite generators and relations proof; image-subalgebra refinement by Q82

proof.text: The composite $\phi\psi$ fixes $S$ and every $d_a$, hence fixes every polynomial in the $d_a$ and is $\mathrm{id}_D$. For $h\in H$ choose a polynomial $p\in S_i[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ with $h=p(x)$. Then $\psi(\bar h)=p(x\otimes1)=h\otimes1$, by the balancing relation on each coefficient. Thus $\psi\phi(h\otimes s)=\psi(\bar h s)=(h\otimes1)(1\otimes s)=h\otimes s$. Pure tensors generate $T$ as a module [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so $\psi\phi=\mathrm{id}_T$. The displayed canonical map is therefore an isomorphism of $S$-algebras, and $H$ has all the required properties.
